description: The golden corpus for the discovery.v1 wire contract. This manifest is the SINGLE inventory: the Go and Python runners read THIS file over THESE fixtures (G-70). `reject_by_client` documents are valid against the schema and refused by ParseDiscovery / parse_discovery, because they need a comparison JSON Schema cannot make. A shared trusted-issuer mismatch (a valid document whose issuer is not the configured one) is asserted in both runners directly, since the trusted issuer is configuration, not a document.

accept.why: The ordinary document: bare https origin, jwks_uri at the fixed path.
An issuer with an explicit port and a path prefix. The jwks_uri carries the same prefix: the path of the issuer is part of its identity, not decoration.

reject.why: No issuer. Discovery without an issuer cannot be bound to the URL it was fetched from.
No jwks_uri: a verifier would have no JWKS to read.
No dev_health_key_use. A document that does not say which key use it describes cannot be told apart from another issuer's, so the member is required rather than defaulted.
No algorithm list; the contract requires the verifier to be told EdDSA, not left to assume.
Plain http issuer. Refused at the wire-format level (see the schema description for local-development configuration). Only the issuer is http, so exactly one member trips.
A trailing slash. `https://a` and `https://a/` would be two issuers to a byte comparison and one to a human, which is how a verifier ends up trusting the wrong one.
A query on the issuer, forbidden by OpenID Connect Discovery section 3.
Userinfo in the issuer: a credential-in-URL shape and a classic confusable-host trick.
A jwks_uri at some other path. TRD section 15 fixes the path.
A query on the jwks_uri; the endpoint takes no parameters.
`none` advertised next to EdDSA (TRD section 24: alg=none must be rejected by fixture).
A symmetric algorithm advertised instead of EdDSA.
The ACR Web-assertion key use. TRD section 12: platform token keys and Web-assertion keys are separate issuers; this is a document from the wrong one, and it is refused rather than merely unlikely.
An OpenID endpoint the Auth Control Plane does not offer here. Adding members is a v2 decision.

reject_by_client.why: jwks_uri on another host than the issuer. Valid against the schema (two well-formed https URLs), refused by the client: the issuer disagrees with its own endpoint URL. This is the attack: a document that names a JWKS the issuer does not serve.
Same host, different port. A byte comparison distinguishes it and a host comparison would not; the contract compares the whole string.
The issuer has a path prefix and the jwks_uri sits at the bare origin: a sibling tenant's JWKS on the same host.
The jwks_uri is under the issuer but not at the fixed path directly beneath it. A prefix test would pass this; equality refuses it.
